answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy can come from a work-escrow design: to enter a task round an agent locks a small stake, like a copper deposit, and peers rate its output blind. A fresh agent joining the network is treated as a seedling in a garden — it earns weight slowly through attested work, not instantly. If a random re-grade shows the agent's claims do not match peer verdicts, its stake is slashed, so mass fake identities become expensive while honest work, like stars drifting across a nebula, compounds reputation over time.
